A secreted neuropeptide of the PACAP family acts through G protein-coupled receptors to promote neuronal survival and neuroendocrine responses to stress; a GDNF-family co-receptor transmits artemin signals in sensory and sympathetic neurons; ERBB4 receives neuregulin at synapses and in interneuron development; the delta-2 glutamate receptor subunit is a Purkinje cell synaptic organiser whose loss causes ataxia; and POU4F2 is the transcription factor that commits retinal ganglion cells to their fate.

only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark a perivascular stromal and endothelial compartment, the interface where capillaries meet connective tissue matrix. Secreted matrix components such as EFEMP1 (fibulin-3) and ECM2 organise the basement membrane and elastic fibre environment that keeps vessels and surrounding tissue mechanically coherent, while IL33 acts both as a nuclear factor in endothelium and, when released from damaged cells, as an alarmin that recruits type 2 immune responses.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline an endothelial identity and blood-vessel morphogenesis programme, of the kind that distinguishes vascular endothelium and sets arterial versus venous character during angiogenic remodelling. Its output is a patent, correctly patterned vascular network: guidance receptors such as neuropilin-1 and the fibronectin leucine-rich repeat protein FLRT2 read angiogenic and adhesive cues, adhesion-family GPCRs enriched in endothelium (ADGRL4/ELTD1, ADGRL2) tune sprouting behaviour, and the soluble guanylate cyclase alpha subunit places nitric oxide-cGMP signalling and vessel tone in the same module.
